title: The Massachusetts List of Interchangeable Drugs: its two parts, its exclusions and how it changes
rule_summary: Under M.G.L. c. 17, § 13(b) the drug formulary commission shall prepare a drug formulary of interchangeable drug products, which shall be adopted by regulations of the Department of Public Health, and shall also prepare a drug formulary of chemically equivalent substitutions for drugs that are opiates contained in schedule II or III of M.G.L. c. 94C, § 3 that the commission has determined have a heightened level of public health risk due to the drugs' potential for abuse and misuse, which the Department shall adopt by regulation and which shall include formulations the commission has determined may be appropriately substituted and that incorporate abuse deterrent properties. Said formularies shall not include drugs which are the subject matter of patent rights issued by the United States Patent Office, or drug products for which bioequivalence is considered essential but has not been established by the Food and Drug Administration, and shall be revised not less frequently than once a year. 105 CMR 720.000 establishes the drug formulary, or list of interchangeable drug products, known as the Massachusetts List of Interchangeable Drugs (MLID). Under 105 CMR 720.050 the MLID consists of (1) drug products considered by FDA to be therapeutically equivalent to other pharmaceutically equivalent products listed with the same generic or chemical name according to the most recent edition of Approved Drug Products with Therapeutic Equivalence Evaluations (the Orange Book) and its supplements, and (2) drug products specified on a list established by the Department and set forth in 105 CMR 720.200 (the Additional List) for which the commission has determined that bioequivalence is not essential or, if it may be essential, that bioequivalence has been established. Under 105 CMR 720.060 the following are excluded: drug products for which the Commonwealth has determined that bioequivalence may be essential but for which bioequivalence has not been established; drug products which are the subject matter of patent rights, for which provision by other than the patent holder would violate the patent; and drug products available from only one manufacturer at one price. Under 105 CMR 720.070 products meeting 105 CMR 720.050(1) are deemed interchangeable and added upon publication of the most recent edition of the Orange Book and its supplements, and products meeting 105 CMR 720.050(2) are added through the procedures in 105 CMR 720.080 to 720.090. Under 105 CMR 720.080 the Department, working with the commission, shall review at least once a year and revise as necessary the list adopted under 105 CMR 720.050(2), and has authority to review and revise the list adopted under 105 CMR 720.050(1) as necessary, with those revisions specified on an exception list set forth in 105 CMR 720.200. The appendix at 105 CMR 720.200 describes the lookup: a drug product whose same drug product, dosage form and strength has been assigned an 'A' rating by FDA in the Orange Book and is not listed on the Exception List is interchangeable; a drug product not listed in the Orange Book is looked up by generic name on the Additional List, where the same drug product, dosage form and strength must be listed.
exam_relevance: Tests that interchangeability in Massachusetts is a question of listing in the MLID (the Orange Book therapeutic-equivalence portion, subject to the Exception List, together with the Additional List) and that single-source products, patent-protected products and products whose essential bioequivalence has not been established are excluded.

numeric_facts.fact: Department and commission review of the Additional List
numeric_facts.conditions: 105 CMR 720.080: at least once a year, revising as necessary

exceptions: Excluded from the MLID under 105 CMR 720.060: drug products for which bioequivalence may be essential but has not been established; drug products subject to patent rights where provision by other than the patent holder would violate the patent; and drug products available from only one manufacturer at one price.
Revisions to the Orange Book portion of the MLID are specified on the Exception List set forth in 105 CMR 720.200.
common_confusions: Treating every FDA-approved generic as interchangeable in Massachusetts. The Orange Book portion is the products FDA considers therapeutically equivalent, subject to revision through the Exception List, and anything else must appear on the Additional List.
Assuming a product from a single manufacturer can be interchanged. Products available from only one manufacturer at one price are excluded.
Treating the formulary of interchangeable drug products and the formulary of abuse deterrent substitutions for schedule II or III opiates as one list. M.G.L. c. 17, § 13(b) provides for each.
